Body: The new `connected` signal is only ever set to `true` on `server.connected` and is never reset to `false` when the SSE stream disconnects/reconnects (the `while (true)` resubscribe loop). This can leave `connected()` stuck true during reconnect attempts, which defeats its purpose for gating message sends while the event loop isn’t consuming events. Consider setting `connected` to `false` when entering a (re)connect attempt and/or when the `for await` loop ends, and then back to `true` when `server.connected` is observed again.

This `/event` SSE ordering change is addressing a subtle race (first prompt response events getting dropped). There are already endpoint tests using `Server.App()` in `packages/opencode/test/server/*`, but I couldn’t find coverage for this SSE handshake/subscribe ordering. Consider adding an automated test that opens the SSE stream and immediately publishes a bus event (or triggers a prompt) and asserts the client receives it.

**Style suggestion:** The `safe` function is defined at module scope but is only used inside `getUsage`. Per the style guide: "Keep things in one function unless composable or reusable". Consider moving this helper back inside the `getUsage` function where it's used, unless you anticipate reusing it elsewhere in this file.

**Suggestion:** This if-block is currently a no-op (just a TODO comment). Consider either implementing the handling now, or removing the if-block entirely and tracking the TODO elsewhere. Empty conditional blocks can be confusing to future readers.

`win32IgnoreCtrlC()` permanently disables Ctrl+C delivery for the process (and there’s no corresponding restore). That can leave users unable to interrupt the program and can also affect shutdown events. Consider adding a restore function (e.g. call SetConsoleCtrlHandler(NULL, FALSE)) and ensuring it runs on cleanup/exit.

`win32EnforceCtrlCGuard()` is started on mount but never stopped. If the TUI unmounts/remounts or if `tui()` is used in a context that doesn’t hard-exit the process, this will accumulate intervals. Consider capturing the interval id and clearing it in an `onCleanup`/exit handler.

`WEBKIT_DISABLE_DMABUF_RENDERER` is set (if absent) for the X11 and Auto paths, but not for the explicit Wayland path. Previously this flag was applied for the Wayland-without-X11 fallback case as well; dropping it only when forcing Wayland could reintroduce the WebKit/GTK DMABUF issues this code is trying to mitigate. If the intent is to keep the mitigation in place regardless of backend choice, set it (preferably with `set_env_if_absent`) in the Wayland branch too, or document why it should differ.

`default_use_decorations()` disables decorations for any "known tiling session" before checking whether the session is Wayland (`is_wayland_session`). This means decorations will also be disabled for X11 tiling WMs (e.g. i3/bspwm) even though the PR description only mentions changing decoration behavior for tiling *Wayland* sessions. If X11 is not intended to change, gate the tiling-WM decoration disablement behind `is_wayland_session(env)` (or update the PR description to reflect that this affects X11 sessions too).
Fixed in f4a0e6fa2. Added `WEBKIT_DISABLE_DMABUF_RENDERER` with `set_env_if_absent` in the explicit Wayland branch as well, so mitigation is applied consistently.
Adjusted in f4a0e6fa2. Decorations now default to off for i3 sessions even on X11, while non-tiling X11 remains decorated by default. PR description has been updated to reflect this behavior.
Fixed in f4a0e6fa2. `configure_display_backend()` now preserves caller-provided `WINIT_UNIX_BACKEND` and `GDK_BACKEND` by using `set_env_if_absent` instead of unconditional overwrite.

The `last_updated` field is not part of the Provider.Model type schema. According to the Provider.Model zod schema (defined in provider.ts), only `release_date` is a valid field. This field should be removed as it will either cause a type error or be silently ignored at runtime.
```suggestion

```

The fallback model is being created by spreading properties from the source model, but critical required fields may be missing or incorrect. The Provider.Model type requires fields like `providerID`, `capabilities`, `limit`, `status`, `options`, and `headers`. If the source model is from a different provider (e.g., has `providerID: "openai"`), the fallback model will inherit the wrong `providerID`. Consider explicitly setting all required fields rather than relying on spread operator, similar to how it's done in codex.ts (lines 375-403).

The new `ensureGpt53Codex` function lacks test coverage. Given that the codebase has comprehensive tests for similar functionality (e.g., test/plugin/codex.test.ts), consider adding tests to verify: (1) the function correctly creates a fallback model when gpt-5.3-codex is missing, (2) it returns early when gpt-5.3-codex already exists, (3) it returns early when no suitable source model is available, and (4) the created model has the correct properties including variants.

The model name "GPT-5.3-Codex" (with a hyphen) is inconsistent with the naming convention used in codex.ts, which uses "GPT-5.3 Codex" (with a space) for the same model. For consistency across the codebase, the name should be "GPT-5.3 Codex".
```suggestion

```

The “default behavior (enabled)” assertion depends on the external environment already not having `OPENCODE_PS4_CONTROLLER="false"`, which can make the test fail on some machines/CI configurations. Save the original env var value at the start of the test (or in a `beforeEach`), set it explicitly for each scenario, and restore it in an `afterEach`/finally block.

This test only asserts properties of a locally-declared object, so it will still pass even if the plugin implementation changes or breaks (it doesn’t validate the plugin at all). Consider exercising behavior from `PS4ControllerPlugin` (e.g., invoke the returned `"experimental.chat.system.transform"` hook and assert it pushes controller hints when enabled), or expose/export the mapping constants from the plugin and assert against those.
```suggestion

```

Using fixed ports (18000–18003) makes the tests prone to failing when those ports are already in use on the test runner. Prefer selecting an ephemeral/free port at runtime (or allow `ensureRunning` to accept port `0` if supported), then assert `isRunning()` and/or the resolved bound port.

The global `response` queue has no correlation to a specific request, so concurrent `callTui(...)` invocations can receive mismatched responses (whoever awaits `response.next()` first gets the next posted response). To make this safe under concurrency, include a request id with each queued request and require `/response` to provide that id, then route responses to the correct awaiting caller (e.g., a `Map<id, Deferred>`).
The markdown table syntax is incorrect (`||` prefixes each row), which will render poorly or not as a table in many viewers. Replace with standard pipe table syntax using single `|` delimiters.

The plugin implementation does not expose an `event` hook; it directly subscribes to `Bus` internally. Update the docs to reflect the actual hooks returned (`permission.ask`, `experimental.chat.system.transform`) and optionally document the internal `Bus.subscribe(...)` behavior separately.
```suggestion
- **permission.ask**: Triggers vibration when permissions are requested
- **experimental.chat.system.transform**: Adds controller information to system prompts

Internally, the plugin also subscribes to the OpenCode event bus (for example, via `Bus.subscribe(...)`) to listen for events and drive controller feedback, but this internal subscription is not exposed as a separate public hook.
```

This branch checks for `$HASH_PATH/node_modules` but hashes `$HASH_PATH` instead of the `node_modules` directory, which can produce an incorrect hash and lead to persistent Nix hash mismatches. Hash the same path that corresponds to the fixed-output contents (likely `$HASH_PATH/node_modules`, or otherwise the exact output root used by the derivation).
```suggestion
        CORRECT_HASH=$(nix hash path --sri "$HASH_PATH/node_modules" 2>/dev/null || true)
```

When invoking `wsl -e <app> <path>`, consider inserting an explicit option terminator (e.g., `--`) before the path (if the target CLIs support it). Otherwise a valid filename starting with `-` could be interpreted as a flag by the app, which is an argument-injection vector even though the shell isn’t involved.
```suggestion
                const result = await Command.create("wsl", ["-e", app, "--", linuxPath]).execute() // arguments are passed as separate array elements to avoid shell interpretation and injection attacks; `--` prevents filenames starting with `-` from being treated as flags
```

`allowed` and `validPattern` are recreated on every `openPath` call. Consider hoisting them to module scope (or at least outside the function) so they’re allocated once and the policy is easier to audit/change.

The environment variable is read twice: once into the `copy` variable (line 40) and again inside the `truthy()` function (line 42). While this is functionally correct, it's inefficient and confusing. Consider inlining the truthy logic to avoid the redundant environment variable read: `copy === undefined ? process.platform === "win32" : (copy.toLowerCase() === "true" || copy.toLowerCase() === "1")`
```suggestion
    copy === undefined
      ? process.platform === "win32"
      : copy.toLowerCase() === "true" || copy.toLowerCase() === "1"
```

`bool(key, fallback)` applies `fallback` not only when the env var is unset, but also when it is set to an unrecognized value. This changes the previous behavior for `OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL_DISABLE_COPY_ON_SELECT`: on Windows, values like an empty string or "foo" will now evaluate to the Windows default (`true`) instead of `false`. Consider only using `fallback` when the env var is `undefined` (or empty, if desired), and treating unrecognized values consistently (e.g., as `false` or as a separate configurable behavior).

`github-copilot-enterprise` is cloned from `github-copilot` *before* config provider/model overrides are applied (see earlier creation of `database["github-copilot-enterprise"]`). That means user-defined/copied models added under `provider.github-copilot.models` in config will not appear under `github-copilot-enterprise`, even though this loop tries to patch both providers. Consider rebuilding/refreshing the enterprise provider after config processing (or cloning lazily) so both providers see the same post-config model set.

This change introduces important behavior for config-defined Copilot models (forcing `model.api.npm` to `@ai-sdk/github-copilot` after config parsing), but there doesn’t appear to be a unit test covering it. Only the `test` script passes `--timeout 30000`. This package also runs tests via `bun test --coverage` in the `lint` script, which will still use Bun’s default 5000ms timeout and can fail for tests that install dependencies (e.g. `Config.waitForDependencies()` in `test/config/config.test.ts`). Consider adding the same `--timeout 30000` flag there (or factoring a shared base test command) to keep test execution consistent.

The comment says “timeout is not actually parsed from bunfig.toml”, but it’s specifically the `[test].timeout` field that Bun currently ignores (while `[test].preload` is still used). Consider rewording to avoid implying Bun ignores the whole bunfig file, and (optionally) mention the Bun version(s) affected for future readers.
```suggestion
# Note: [test].timeout is not currently parsed from bunfig.toml (see src/bunfig.zig in oven-sh/bun),
# so we use --timeout in package.json scripts instead. [test].preload is still honored.
# See: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/issues/7789
```

Using the SQLite DB file itself (`opencode.db`) as the migration marker becomes unsafe once `serve` skips migration: `opencode serve` can still create `opencode.db` later (via `Database.Client()` on first request), which will permanently prevent the JSON->SQLite migration from ever running in future interactive CLI invocations (because the marker now exists). Consider switching the guard to a dedicated "migration completed" marker (e.g., a separate file or a row in a meta table), or keying the decision off presence of the legacy JSON storage directory instead of DB existence so the migration can still run later when appropriate.
Fixed - now uses a dedicated `migration.json` marker file that's only written after migration completes successfully.

The fallback logic for handling anyOf/oneOf with type variants may produce unexpected results. When multiple type variants exist, selecting only the first variant discards the other variants without considering whether they represent compatible types or important constraints. For example, if anyOf contains [{"type": "string", "minLength": 5}, {"type": "string", "maxLength": 10}], only the minLength constraint would be preserved. Consider whether this behavior is acceptable for Gemini API compatibility, or if a more sophisticated merge strategy is needed.

The code strips allOf, anyOf, and oneOf keywords from the schema but does not handle allOf which could be used to merge schemas. Unlike anyOf/oneOf which represent alternatives, allOf represents a combination of all schemas and could potentially be merged into a single schema object. Consider adding logic to handle allOf by merging its array elements into the parent schema, similar to how anyOf/oneOf with const values are handled.

When anyOf/oneOf contains a mix of const values and other schema types (e.g., [{"const": "foo"}, {"type": "string"}]), the const values are extracted but the logic checks if constValues.length === variants.length. This means mixed arrays are not converted to enum, and the variants are later stripped entirely on line 939-940. This could result in loss of schema information. Consider logging a warning when schema information is being discarded, or implementing a more graceful degradation strategy.

When converting anyOf/oneOf with const values to enum, the description field from individual const objects is lost. For example, {"anyOf": [{"const": "append", "description": "Add to end"}, {"const": "prepend", "description": "Add to start"}]} becomes {"type": "string", "enum": ["append", "prepend"]} without preserving the descriptions for each enum value. Consider preserving the parent description if it exists, or documenting that per-value descriptions cannot be represented in Gemini's enum format.

The code strips the "default" keyword which may result in loss of default values that could be useful for API consumers. According to issue #12295, Gemini allows "default" alongside $ref, suggesting it may be supported in some contexts. Consider verifying through testing whether "default" needs to be stripped in all contexts or only in specific ones, and document the reasoning for stripping it if it's necessary for API compatibility.

The new functionality for handling anyOf/oneOf with const values, stripping unsupported keywords, and inferring type: "object" lacks test coverage. While the test file packages/opencode/test/provider/transform.test.ts contains tests for other Gemini schema transformations, there are no tests verifying:
1. Conversion of anyOf/oneOf with const values to enum
2. Stripping of the 28 newly-added unsupported keywords (additionalProperties, $ref, $schema, etc.)
3. Type inference when properties/required exist without type

Consider adding comprehensive tests for these new behaviors to prevent regressions.

The code strips $ref without resolving it to the referenced schema. Issue #12295 mentions that Gemini API rejects schemas containing $ref references and expects them to be expanded. Simply removing $ref will result in an incomplete schema (e.g., {"$ref": "#/$defs/MyType", "description": "..."} becomes just {"description": "..."}). To properly fix this issue, $ref should be resolved by looking up the reference in $defs/definitions and merging the referenced schema into the current location before stripping occurs.

The Preview/Source toggle is rendered for any `.md/.markdown` path, even if the file content is treated as binary. In that case the Switch will render the binary placeholder, but the toggle still appears (and Preview can never show). Consider including `!isBinary()` (and any other non-previewable states) in the toggle’s `<Show>` condition so it only appears when a markdown preview can actually be rendered.
```suggestion
      <Show when={state()?.loaded && isMarkdown() && !isBinary()}>
```

When `previewMode()` is true, the code viewer (`renderCode`) is not mounted, which also removes line selection + inline comment rendering. As a result, if `props.comments.focus()` targets a markdown file (e.g. navigating to an existing comment), the focused comment won’t be visible until the user manually switches to Source. Consider auto-switching to Source when a focused comment is for the current file (or when there are existing comments for the file) to preserve the existing focus/navigation behavior.
